title: skills/objectstack-formula: say that == / != on a list-valued field (multiselect, tags, a multiple: true field) is refused, and teach in / exists instead
body:
repo:objectstack#4 · os-project-manager · session_01FEkQ5krBqrrgxCYgjXmfbv

Filing gate ① · Source: fleet · follow-up owed by PR #36207 (Part of #36167; its body declares `Skills-docs: follow-up owed — skills/objectstack-formula/SKILL.md`).

## What happens
Once PR #36207 lands, `validateExpression` refuses `==` / `!=` when one side is a list-valued field: a list type (multiselect, checkboxes, tags) or a select / lookup / user field declared `multiple: true`. CEL answers such a comparison as a constant, so it never or always matches. `skills/objectstack-formula/SKILL.md` lists `==` / `!=` in its operator table (l.77) and shows equality examples (l.131-136), but it says nothing about list subjects. An agent following the skill will author a condition the validator now refuses.

## Done when
The skill's operator table, or a short note beside it, says that `==` / `!=` on a list-valued field is refused, and shows the membership form (`'x' in record.tags`, `record.tags.exists(t, t == 'x')`) with the refusal it replaces. Add an eval case if the skills lane requires one.

reach: the published `objectstack-formula` skill, read by every authoring agent. The text was read at origin/main.
Business reason: agents writing conditions on multi-value fields hit a validation refusal with no guidance in the skill.
Reader: domain:skills lane.
Dedupe: `objectstack-formula list equality` → 0 hits.
Grade: p2. It is a documentation companion to the p1 narrowing (#36167) and lands after #36207 merges.
